You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The fed funds rate is 0.91%, which fits mid-2017 (the effective rate was about 0.91% in Mar-Apr 2017, then 1.16% after the June hike). Unemployment of 4.5% doesn't match May 2017 (4.3%) but would match March 2017 (4.5% as first reported, since later revised to 4.4%). The 10-year yield at 2.30% fits April 2017 or possibly late March. The 2-year at 1.25% fits April 2017. The VIX at 10.36 fits April 2017, which ended near 10.8.

The fed funds rate rose by 0.35 over 3 months, from about 0.55 in January to 0.91. That fits a March hike, which pushed the effective rate to 0.91 in March and April. The unemployment rate was 4.4% in April 2017, and was 4.5% in the data known at the time for March.

The 3-month change in the 10-year yield of -0.15 puts it at 2.30 against 2.45 three months earlier. At the end of April 2017 the yield was 2.28, and three months earlier, end of January, 2.45. That fits April. Equity 1-month return of +1.1% also fits April (S&P up about 1%). Headline CPI of 2.38% fits March 2017 (2.4%), which was the latest published value in April. Core CPI of 2.0% fits March at 2.0%. So the snapshot is end of April 2017.
